note: Curated retrieval/embeddings tips, one per day, rotated by date. Add entries; keep titles short and bodies one paragraph.

tips.title: TF-IDF is the baseline that never blinks
tips.body: Before reaching for embeddings, score your problem with TF-IDF cosine. It is free, deterministic, and often embarrassingly competitive on keyword-shaped queries.

tips.title: Recall@k is the question, MRR is the ranking
tips.body: Recall@5 asks 'did the answer appear?', MRR asks 'how high?'. RAG needs both: a 100% recall with rank-50 retrieval is still a failed pipeline.

tips.title: Paraphrase queries separate lexical from semantic
tips.body: If every query shares words with its answer doc, lexical wins and you learn nothing. Write paraphrase queries ('bots steal my trades') to see what dense retrieval actually buys.
tips.command: embed-playground compare how do bots steal money from my trades

tips.title: Embeddings are not magic, they are priors
tips.body: A sentence-transformer maps text to a learned prior space. The prior reflects its training data; domain jargon ('flash loan', 'MEV') is where generic models guess wrong.

tips.title: Hybrid is a fusion, not a feature
tips.body: RRF fusion combines rankings, and it is only as good as its weakest tier. Benchmark each tier alone before fusing — a broken lexical tier quietly drags the hybrid down.

tips.title: Pin your embedding model version
tips.body: A newer MiniLM checkpoint can silently re-rank your entire corpus. Record the model id and hash with the benchmark results or your leaderboard is untrustworthy.

tips.title: Normalize inputs before encoding
tips.body: HTML tags, markdown, and full-width punctuation corrupt embeddings. Clean both corpus and queries through the same pipeline or you measure your parser, not the model.

tips.title: Chunking is a retrieval decision
tips.body: A paragraph is not a document. Chunk size changes recall more than any model swap; benchmark 128/256/512-token chunks before blaming the encoder.

tips.title: Scores are not probabilities
tips.body: Cosine similarity and RRF scores are ordinal, not calibrated. Thresholds tuned on one corpus fail on the next; evaluate per corpus, per domain.

tips.title: Metadata filters beat bigger models
tips.body: If users always search within a category, filter by category first and rank within it. RAG pipelines that skip structural filters are leaving recall on the table.

tips.title: Test with queries nobody wrote
tips.body: The queries in your README demo are the ones your system passes. Keep a held-out set of natural, noisy, multi-intent queries for honest evaluation.

tips.title: Zero-shot embeddings need domain probes
tips.body: Before fine-tuning, run a small benchmark (this repo's 16 queries) with the generic model. 75-90% recall is often enough; fine-tuning is for the last 10%.

tips.title: The corpus is the interface
tips.body: Users never see your index, they see your docs. Clean, concrete, one-topic-per-doc writing improves every retrieval metric more than any model change.

tips.title: Determinism is a debugging tool
tips.body: Random ordering or hash-order iteration makes ranking bugs nondeterministic. Sort by score, then id, and golden-test the top of the list.

tips.title: MRR gaming is real
tips.body: Short queries with exactly one obvious doc inflate MRR. Mix multi-relevant queries (like this repo's cross-context items) or the metric flatters your demo.

tips.title: Fallbacks keep CI honest
tips.body: A dense tier that needs a 90MB download cannot run in every CI. Keep the lexical tier as the offline golden path and treat dense as an optional accelerator.

tips.title: Watch the long tail of the corpus
tips.body: Embedding quality concentrates on frequent concepts. Measure recall per category; the category with the worst recall is your data problem, not your model problem.

tips.title: Rerankers change the game
tips.body: Cross-encoder rerankers on the top-50 retire most hybrid tuning fights. First retrieval breadth (recall@50), then rerank precision — never the reverse.

tips.title: Snippet quality is a ranking signal
tips.body: A perfect hit with an unreadable snippet loses the user. Keep extraction clean: title, category, and a 1-2 sentence window, like this playground's table.

tips.title: Evaluation belongs in the repo
tips.body: A benchmark script next to the code means every PR can regress retrieval. Golden numbers in tests turn silent ranking drift into a failed build.

tips.title: Document your negative results
tips.body: 'Dense missed q03, lexical missed q02' is the most valuable paragraph in your README. It teaches users where each tier fails — that is how tools get trusted.

tips.title: Query rewriting is preprocessing
tips.body: Users type fragments ('flash loan how'), models expect sentences. Cheap normalization — case, stopwords, expansion of common abbreviations — buys consistent gains.

tips.title: Latency is a benchmark metric
tips.body: Dense search on 36 docs is instant; on 36 million it is an index problem. Record time-per-query in every eval run before scaling claims get made.
